---
title: AI Studio retention
description: The Cron Control job that deletes AI Studio request metadata after 365 days and expired prompt content, with a counts-only dry run, a kill switch and a bounded batch.
updatedAt: "2026-11-03"
audience: developers
---

## Decision

The privacy policy states that AI request metadata is deleted after **365 days**
by default (workspace policies may set 30–2555 days). Captured prompt and
output content carries its own `expires_at` (content retention, default 30
days) and is deleted once that passes. The Cron Control job
`ai-studio-retention` enforces this daily at **02:43 GMT+7** (`43 19 * * *`).
It ships in **dry-run**: no data writes; one counts-only log row, until a reviewed change sets
`AI_STUDIO_RETENTION_MODE` to `delete`.

## Scope

| Store | Action | Due when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `private.ai_studio_run_content` (prompt, output, tool arguments and results) | Row deleted | `expires_at <= now()` |
| `private.ai_studio_runs` (request metadata) | Row deleted | `created_at` older than the workspace's metadata window (default 365 days) |
| `private.ai_studio_run_steps`, `private.ai_studio_usage`, content of a due run | Cascade with the run | With the run |
| `private.ai_studio_evaluation_results.run_id` | Set to null (row kept) | With the run |

Never touched:

- The customer workspace covered by the never-write rule (listed in the
  migration, as in the Meet transcript purge).
- Runs still `reserved` or `running` (credit settlement in flight).
- Runs created in the current calendar month, or with dependent usage settled in that month. The workspace monthly credit budget
  sums `private.ai_studio_usage` from the start of the month, so a 30-day policy
  must not shrink it.
- The credit ledger: `public.ai_credit_transactions`,
  `public.workspace_ai_credit_balances`, `private.ai_credit_reservations` and API
  key counters. None has a foreign key to runs.
- Other AI stores (chat messages, Meet AI, memories) and everything outside
  AI Studio.

## Design

| Function (service_role only, `SECURITY INVOKER`, `search_path = pg_catalog, pg_temp`) | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `private.count_ai_studio_retention()` | `STABLE` preview: counts per table, oldest/newest timestamps and cutoffs. No content or identifiers |
| `private.cleanup_ai_studio_retention_batch(p_limit 1..1000)` | Deletes at most `p_limit` expired content rows and at most `p_limit` due runs, oldest first, `SKIP LOCKED`, and returns counts and `more`/`done`/`locked` |
| `private.record_ai_studio_retention_run(...)` | Inserts one counts-only row into `private.ai_studio_retention_runs` |
| `private.ai_studio_metadata_cutoff(days, now)` | `least(now - days, start of month)` |

`private.cleanup_ai_studio_retention()` (the original unbounded function) is
unchanged and not scheduled.

Content categories are determined by expiry, regardless of deletion path:
`content_rows` includes every expired row removed directly or by cascade;
`cascade_content_rows` includes only unexpired content removed with a due run.
Only the directly selected expired rows and parent runs have a per-batch limit;
expired content removed by cascade is additional. Preview and summed batch
categories reconcile on a static snapshot.

The batch locks eligible runs before limiting. A nonempty remainder after a
partial batch returns `locked`, which the Worker records as a failed incomplete
run without retrying in the same invocation. The next daily run resumes it.

The Worker side is `apps/cron-control/src/processors/ai-studio-retention.ts`:

- `AI_STUDIO_RETENTION_MODE=off`: kill switch, no database call.
- Exact `dry-run` (the configured default): no data writes; one counts-only log row.
- Any unrecognised raw value, including unset, whitespace and case variants: off, with a code-only warning.
- `delete`: up to 40 batches of 500 per run, checking the Cron Control stop fence
  and a 25-second time reserve before each. No in-run retry; the next day
  continues from the remaining data.

Every non-off run writes one row to `private.ai_studio_retention_runs` (mode, status,
batches and counts). A run whose log cannot be written is `failed`; five failed
or unknown days stop the job durably in the Cron Control ledger.

## Cost bounds

| Bound | Per run (one a day) |
| --- | --- |
| Database requests | Dry run 2; delete at most 41 |
| Rows deleted | At most 20,000 directly selected content rows and 20,000 runs (plus their cascade) |
| Processor time | 300 seconds |

## Enablement

1. Database owner records a backup point (PITR) and applies the migration.
2. Deploy Cron Control. The job is enabled in dry-run.
3. After the first 02:43 GMT+7 run, read the counts:
   ```sql
   select recorded_at, mode, status, content_rows, run_rows,
     cascade_content_rows, step_rows, usage_rows, evaluation_links,
     held_in_flight_runs, held_current_month_runs
   from private.ai_studio_retention_runs order by recorded_at desc limit 5;
   ```
   or once, read-only: `begin read only; select private.count_ai_studio_retention(); rollback;`
4. After sign-off, a reviewed change sets `AI_STUDIO_RETENTION_MODE` to
   `delete`. Read the next run's row back and leave the schedule on.

## Stop and rollback

- Fastest stop: `POST /control/jobs/ai-studio-retention/stop` (operator token).
  An in-flight batch can still commit at most 500 rows per table.
- Database stop without a deploy:
  `revoke execute on function private.cleanup_ai_studio_retention_batch(integer) from service_role;`
  The next batch fails and the run is recorded `failed`.
- Config: `AI_STUDIO_RETENTION_MODE` back to `dry-run` or `off`, or remove the
  job from `CRON_CONTROL_ENABLED_JOBS`.
- `apps/database/rollbacks/20261103110000_ai_studio_retention_schedule.rollback.sql`
  drops the new functions and keeps the counts-only run log.

**Deleted rows cannot be restored by any switch or rollback**, only from the
backup taken before the first deleting run.

## Regression evidence

- `apps/database/supabase/tests/ai-studio-retention-schedule.sql`: grants,
  invoker rights and pinned search path, the month-floor cutoff, the 365-day
  default and a 30-day override, the batch limit, oldest-first order, cascades,
  evaluation links cleared, in-flight, current-month and never-write workspace rows kept,
  credit ledger untouched, idempotent re-run, and counts-only outputs.
- `apps/database/scripts/ai-studio-retention-concurrency.mjs`: two real sessions
  against a disposable Supabase PG17 container. Run with `node <script> <supabase_db_tt-...>`;
  verifies skipping locked oldest rows, deleting later unlocked rows, and lock exhaustion.
- `apps/cron-control/src/ai-studio-retention.test.ts`: registration and
  schedule, dry-run by default (count only), unrecognised raw modes stay off,
  the `off` kill switch, bounded delete loop, batch and time budgets, operator
  stop, out-of-bounds summaries, failures and the run log.
